verdict.summary: You can create a Clio Manage Developer Application yourself and connect your own Clio account in minutes. Getting listed in the Clio App Directory takes a security and compliance questionnaire, a demo with Clio's API Partnerships team, and a listing sign-off. Clio does not publish a timeline for any of this. The pages read also don't say whether an unlisted app can be used by any Clio user.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min to reach a working connection; 1-3 days of work for the questionnaire, demo and listing
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account. App Directory review time is not documented.

gates.name: Developer Application (your own Clio account)
gates.unlocks: You create a Developer Application in the Clio Developer Portal, get the app key and secret, and authorize your own Clio Manage account through Composio.
limits: Access tokens expire after 30 days (expires_in 2592000); use the refresh token to renew them
Default rate limit is 50 requests/min per access token at peak hours
Each region (e.g. app.clio.com vs eu.app.clio.com) needs its own Clio account and its own Developer Application

gates.name: Unlisted app authorized by other Clio users
gates.unlocks: Other Clio Manage users (for example a pilot law firm) go through the same authorize URL and approve your app on Clio's OAuth approval page.
limits: Install caps or restrictions for unreviewed apps are not documented (see open questions)
What each user can access is also limited by their own Clio role, even if your app has the permission
If you change permissions, existing users must reauthorize
gates.time_to_reach: Probably immediate after Gate 1. Not confirmed: Clio's docs don't describe any install caps or allowlists for unlisted apps.

gates.name: Clio App Directory listing
gates.unlocks: Your integration is published in the Clio App Directory after security approval, a demo, and listing sign-off.
limits: Clio's Application Security and Compliance team must approve your answers to their questionnaire
You need a successful demo with the API Partnerships team
Your listing must follow the App Directory Listing Guidelines
gates.time_to_reach: Not documented (several manual steps: questionnaire, demo, listing draft)

steps.title: Sign in to the Clio Manage Developer Portal
steps.detail: Go to developers.clio.com and sign in with your Clio account. This is the Manage portal. The Clio Platform/Grow portal at developers.api.clio.com is a different product with a different review process.
gotchas: The portal login is a regular Clio account login. If you don't have a Clio account, you need one first.
The docs don't say whether a paid or admin account is required.

steps.title: Pick the region(s) you'll support
steps.detail: Decide which Clio regions your users are in (for example US app.clio.com or EU eu.app.clio.com). Each region needs its own Clio account and its own Developer Application, and app IDs differ between regions.
gotchas: An app from one region won't work for users in another. You need a separate Composio auth config per region.

steps.title: Create the Developer Application
steps.detail: Create a new Developer Application. Required fields are Name and Website URL. Description, icons, support URL and deauthorization callback URL are optional. Users see the name, icon, description and website on Clio's OAuth approval page, so fill them in carefully.

values.label: Name
values.value: Your product name (shown on the OAuth approval page)

steps.title: Add the redirect URI
steps.detail: In the app's redirect URIs field, paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config. The redirect_uri in the authorize request must exactly match one of the URLs registered here.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

steps.title: Select app permissions and accept the Developer Terms
steps.detail: Choose the permissions your agent needs, then accept the Developer Terms of Service. Both are required. Permissions are locked in when a user authorizes, so plan the full set now to avoid asking users to reauthorize later.
gotchas: If you change permissions later, every existing user has to reauthorize.
A user's Clio role can still block resources your app has permission for.

steps.title: Copy the app key and secret into a Composio custom auth config
steps.detail: Composio has no managed Clio app, so create a custom OAuth auth config and enter the Developer Application's app key (client_id) and secret (client_secret). For US apps the endpoints are https://app.clio.com/oauth/authorize and https://app.clio.com/oauth/token.
gotchas: The authorize endpoint doesn't reject a wrong client_id up front. It just shows the Clio login page, so typos only show up later in the flow.

steps.title: Run a test authorization with your own account
steps.detail: Start a connection through Composio, sign in to Clio, approve the app, and check that the token exchange returns an access token (expires_in 2592000) and a refresh token. Then make one API call to confirm your permissions work.

steps.title: Add token refresh and rate-limit backoff
steps.detail: Access tokens last 30 days, so make sure refresh is handled. Limit requests to about 50 per minute per access token at peak hours, and back off when you get HTTP 429 Too Many Requests.

steps.title: Pilot with invited Clio users
steps.detail: Have a few external Clio users (for example a pilot firm) connect through your Composio flow. Check that their Clio roles give them access to the resources your agent uses.
gotchas: The docs don't say whether unlisted apps have install caps.

steps.title: Request a security review and complete Clio's questionnaire
steps.detail: Follow Clio's 'Launch your app' handbook to start the App Directory process. Clio will send you its security and compliance questionnaire. An agent can draft the answers from your architecture, data handling and security documents. You review them and submit.
gotchas: The handbook's Manage-specific steps for requesting the review were not fully read. The Grow/Platform flow (apply from the app details page) is different.

steps.title: Wait for Application Security and Compliance approval
steps.detail: Clio's Application Security and Compliance team reviews your questionnaire. Clio does not publish a timeline.

steps.title: Email API Partnerships to schedule a demo
steps.detail: After security approval, email Clio's API Partnerships team to schedule a demo, then present the integration.

steps.title: Complete the App Directory listing form and approve the draft
steps.detail: After a successful demo, API Partnerships sends you a listing form. An agent can draft the listing content using the App Directory Listing Guidelines. Clio then drafts the listing page, and you review it and sign off so they can publish.
gotchas: Signing off on the final listing has to be done by you.

requirements.item: Clio account in each region you support
requirements.detail: You need a Clio login to use the Developer Portal, and each region needs its own account and Developer Application.
Both are required fields and appear on the OAuth approval page.
It must exactly match the redirect_uri Composio sends.

requirements.item: Accept the Developer Terms of Service
requirements.detail: Required before you can build an integration.
Clio's Application Security and Compliance team must review and approve it before you can be listed.
A successful demo is required before you get the listing form.

requirements.item: Listing that meets the App Directory Listing Guidelines
requirements.detail: Clio drafts the listing from your form and publishes it after you sign off.

scopes.scope: App permissions (selected in the Developer Application form)
scopes.effect: Permissions are set in the app form and requested as a space-separated scope list. They're fixed when a user authorizes, so changing them means users must reauthorize. A user's Clio role can still restrict access. The specific scope names and whether any of them trigger extra review were not found.

blockers.symptom: Authorization fails because of a redirect URI mismatch
blockers.cause: The redirect_uri in the request doesn't match any redirect URL registered in the app settings.
blockers.fix: Paste the exact Composio callback URL into the app's redirect URIs and save.

blockers.cause: You went over the default limit of about 50 requests per minute per access token at peak hours.
blockers.fix: Back off and retry, and throttle your agent's calls.

blockers.symptom: A resource is unavailable even though the app has the permission
blockers.cause: The authorizing user's Clio Manage role restricts access to it.
blockers.fix: Have a user with the right role authorize, or adjust the user's role in Clio.

blockers.symptom: New permissions don't apply to existing connections
blockers.cause: Permissions are fixed when the user authorizes.
blockers.fix: Ask users to reauthorize after you change permissions.

blockers.symptom: Users in another region (e.g. EU) can't connect
blockers.cause: Each region needs its own Developer Application, and app IDs differ between regions.
blockers.fix: Create an app in each region and a separate Composio auth config for each.

blockers.symptom: Login page appears instead of an error when the client_id is wrong
blockers.cause: The authorize endpoint doesn't reject unknown clients up front.
blockers.fix: Double-check the app key in your Composio auth config.

blockers.symptom: Public distribution may require a partnership
blockers.cause: A third-party source (not Clio) says public use requires a partnership and marketplace approval.
blockers.fix: Plan for the security questionnaire and demo if you need wide distribution, and confirm with Clio API Partnerships.
blockers.contact: Clio API Partnerships team (via the Launch your app handbook)

composio.note: Composio has no Clio toolkit or managed OAuth app, so there's no managed option to start with. You have to register your own Clio Manage Developer Application (one per region) and enter its app key and secret in a custom Composio auth config, with Composio's callback URL as the redirect URI.

open_questions: Can any Clio user authorize an unlisted, unreviewed app, or are there install caps or restrictions? Neither was documented.
What are the Manage scope names, and do any of them trigger extra review?
Does Clio Manage support PKCE? It was only confirmed for Clio Platform/Grow.
What are the refresh token expiry and rotation rules?
How long do the security review, demo scheduling and listing take? Is a privacy policy, logo, minimum install count or demo video required?
How exactly do you request the Manage-specific security review? The handbook section was only partly read.
Does the Clio account used for the Developer Portal need to be paid or an admin account?
What are Clio's common reasons for rejecting an app?
